round1_a.scope: Home, MemoDetail, Setting and their dialogs/tabs; other launch sites inspected only to resolve shared ownership.

screens.name: Home
screens.reason: A memo collection workspace with its own browsing/filtering context. List/grid and filter variants remain this one place.

screens.name: Memo detail
screens.reason: Reads one selected memo, its comments and connections. Arrival from Home, other collections, parent links or backlinks does not make the destination a child of its launcher.

screens.name: Memo editor
screens.reason: One draft-working place shared by inline composition, memo editing, comment composition and the global composer. The draft is its persistent process; presentation and new/edit/comment conditions do not create separate Screen identities.

screens.name: Link memo
screens.reason: Searches and selects another memo for the current draft. Selection modifies that retained draft, so this subdivides the editor process rather than the page hosting it.

screens.name: Memo location
screens.reason: Collects location coordinates and place details for the retained draft. Ending or replacing the draft ends or changes this context.

screens.name: Move memo
screens.reason: Selects destination space and visibility for a chosen memo. Home cards and the detail reading share this destination, so it belongs once at their common Experience.

screens.name: Memo share links
screens.reason: Lists, creates and revokes links for the memo currently selected in its reading; the memoName follows that persistent subject.

screens.name: Memo share image
screens.reason: Produces and downloads/shares an image of the memo being read. The scoped implementation exposes this through the detail reading, and its memo comes from that reading context.

screens.name: Attachment preview
screens.reason: Shared media-reading destination reached from memo cards, memo detail, editor attachments and the attachment collection. Selected media and optional metadata disclosure remain one Screen.

screens.name: Quick find
screens.reason: Shared search-input destination. Its text/expression modes collect alternative query representations for the same browsing action, not separate Screens.

screens.name: Create space
screens.reason: One creation destination shared by Spaces settings and the global space switcher; the list that opens it does not own it.

screens.name: My account
screens.reason: Reads the signed-in account and offers its account maintenance operations. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Spaces
screens.reason: Lists spaces and received invitations, and accepts or declines invitations. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Access tokens
screens.reason: Lists and revokes the signed-in account's tokens. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Preferences
screens.reason: Changes personal defaults, language and media metadata preferences. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Webhooks
screens.reason: Lists and manages the signed-in account's webhooks. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Members
screens.reason: Lists instance users and manages roles, status and deletion. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: System settings
screens.reason: Reads and changes instance-wide general settings. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Memo settings
screens.reason: Changes instance memo settings, limits and reaction options. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Tag settings
screens.reason: Maintains personal tag matching and content-blur settings. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Memo import and export
screens.reason: Exports memos and starts a staged import. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Storage settings
screens.reason: Configures the storage destination and upload limits. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Notification settings

screens.name: AI settings

screens.name: Resource statistics
screens.reason: Reads and refreshes instance resource statistics. The Setting route selects this destination; its shell has no separate retained resource/process and is not an additional Screen.

screens.name: Space detail
screens.reason: A selected space is an independent resource-reading workspace reached from space management. It retains space identity while its tabs change; it is not owned by the collection that opens it.

screens.name: Space general
screens.reason: The General tab reads and edits facts of the persistent selected space and exposes leaving/deleting it. Choosing a different space resets this reading.

screens.name: Space members
screens.reason: The Members tab reads members and invitations and changes membership for the same persistent selected space.

screens.name: Invite space member
screens.reason: The retained selected space owns the invitation process. Its space argument, existing members and pending invitations all change with that space; the dialog is rendered outside the tab conditional, so Members is its launch site rather than the persistent owner.

screens.name: Account information
screens.reason: Edits the account retained by My account. The dialog does not select an independent account or serve a second launch context.

screens.name: Account password
screens.reason: Changes the password of the account retained in My account; the user is passed from that reading.

screens.name: Create access token
screens.reason: A new-token process with description and expiry input and one-time token disclosure. The token collection merely opens it and supplies no selected token or continuing creation process.

screens.name: Webhook editor
screens.reason: A chosen webhook or new-webhook draft is the subject, rather than the collection of webhooks. Create/edit and secret disclosure are conditions of one editing destination.

screens.name: Member editor
screens.reason: The dialog establishes the selected user or new-user draft; the member list is only its launcher. Create/edit input differences remain conditions within the editor.

screens.name: Instance profile
screens.reason: Edits the profile of the same instance retained by System settings, a subdivision of that instance configuration context.

screens.name: Identity provider editor
screens.reason: An individual provider or new-provider draft is the editing subject; the SSO list merely opens it. Provider templates and create/edit states remain one destination.

screens.name: AI provider editor
screens.reason: An individual provider draft is selected or created for editing; the AI settings area is a launch site rather than a retained provider workspace.

screens.name: Memo import review
screens.reason: A stage of the retained import process: reads the chosen archive plan and warnings, collects conflict policy and starts import. Cancel/restart ends that staged context.

uncertainties: Settings containment is an authoring question: this inventory models 15 section destinations directly under the Experience and no Settings shell. Source establishes a selector but does not settle whether the product calls configuring settings one persistent process. Nesting all 15 beneath a Settings Screen is a defensible alternative with a materially different ownership tree; the shell would also need its own placed Capability.

The editor is provisionally one shared Screen across inline Home composition, existing memo edits, comments and the global composer. The rubric excludes presentation-only distinctions but source alone cannot settle whether inline draft work is its own place or behavior on each host. That choice changes Screen count and ownership of its link/location dialogs.

Single-launch list-to-editor destinations are provisionally independent Screens (new token, webhook, member, identity-provider and AI-provider editors). Their lists retain no selected resource before launch. Treating each management area as a persistent process would instead nest them, so author confirmation is needed.

Import review is modeled as a nested stage because it retains an archive plan and has policy input. Import completion, access-token disclosure and webhook secret disclosure remain outcomes within their process Screens. The exact point at which a staged condition becomes a distinct place is not fully determined by source.

Screen names are descriptive working names, not author-confirmed product vocabulary. The authenticated Experience is assumed as requested; public share-token and other access contexts are not modeled.

uncertainties: Settings containment is unresolved product meaning: this inventory does not treat the generic Settings dispatcher as a persistent subject/process. An author could identify an enduring settings work process and put its fifteen sections beneath a Settings Screen; the source only shows section selection, and such a container would still need its own placed Capability.

Memo editor identity is a proposed unification of creation, inline edit and comment composition around a persistent draft. The code shares one editor, but shared implementation alone does not prove a single Product place. Splitting those purposes changes both count and ownership of Link Memo and Location and needs an author decision.

Independent form destinations such as member/webhook/identity-provider editors are placed at the Experience because their lists only launch a selected form. Whether a list constitutes an ongoing configuration process is not settled solely by source; treating every list operation as that process would materially change nesting.

Space Detail is retained as the selected-space reading above its two tabs; its header reads the space identity. Exact Scenario placement must leave at least one Capability on that parent rather than only on the tabs.
Image preview and audio player are proposed stable attachment-reading places; their status as Screens rather than controls embedded in an existing reading is an authoring granularity question.

Creation result and import stages are split under the rubric wizard-stage guidance. An author may regard a one-time token reveal or an import report as an Outcome within the same Screen instead; this changes the inventory count.

Scope covers Home, MemoDetail, Settings and their memo/editor/setting dialogs. Other routed pages were inspected only for shared image-preview ownership. Global navigation utilities such as Quick Find and user-preference dialogs were not inventoried as part of those pages; shared global composition and space creation were included because they resolve ownership of scoped forms.

Confirmation dialogs, menus, pickers, inline comments, linked identity rows, account-statistic sections and alternate editor/list drawings remain behavior or components on their host, not additional Screens. No Capability model was authored, so the required at-least-one placed Capability per Screen has not been lint-validated.

uncertainties: Memo editor identity is still unresolved: the implementation uses one editor for inline Home composition, inline memo editing, comments and the global composer. One shared draft-working Screen with nested link/location views remains the provisional reading. The rubric does not establish whether each inline appearance is a separate place or behavior on its host; that changes resource count and the set of qualifying parents.

Management collections versus selected subjects remain ambiguous for new-token, webhook, member, identity-provider and AI-provider editors. I retained their Experience parent because their launch collections select no individual resource beforehand and are not in-progress operations. However those collections can also be read as persistent account or instance contexts: e.g. AccessTokenSection retains currentUser and creates the token with that user as parent. The generic-selector exclusion does not say whether a real resource collection carrying an implicit current account qualifies. Nesting these editors is therefore still defensible.

Nearest qualifying context is not uniquely determined for Invite space member: Space detail explicitly retains the space, while its Members child inherits that same selected space. I retained Space detail because the invitation state is outside the tab conditional and depends on space rather than tab. A reading that the Members tab itself is a persistent membership-management context makes Members the nearest parent. The updated wording gives a nearest rule but does not fully settle qualification for inherited subjects.
Working names are not author-confirmed vocabulary. The authenticated Experience is assumed as requested, and public share-token contexts are outside this scoped experiment.

round2_a.method: Independent reconsideration of every scoped Screen against the revised shipped mapping rubric, followed by targeted read-only inspection of retained space/tab state and process results. No other trial output read; no target code executed or target files modified.

materialChanges: The generic Settings shell alternative is no longer left open: the new explicit exclusion supports the existing 15 sibling section destinations without an extra Settings Screen.
The existing import-review child now has an explicit criterion: retained operation plus Actor policy/confirm input.
Token/secret reveals and import completion are now explicitly excluded as child stages, resolving the earlier staged-condition uncertainty.
Nearest-parent wording exposes a remaining qualification question for Space members versus Space detail; it does not make that assignment unambiguous.
round2Comparison.conclusion: The resulting provisional inventory is unchanged, but confidence improved for Settings and process outcomes. Screen identity and persistent-context qualification still permit materially different trees.

screens.name: edit-account
screens.reason: Edits the account already being read, preserving that account context.

screens.name: change-password
screens.reason: Changes the password of the account already selected in My Account; the only inspected caller is MyAccountSection.

screens.name: create-space
screens.reason: One new-space form shared by the settings collection and global space switcher.

screens.name: space-detail
screens.reason: Selects one space as a persistent subject, replacing the collection reading. The collection is a launch point, not an owning selected subject.

screens.name: space-general
screens.reason: The General tab reads and edits the selected space details and supports leaving/deleting it. The selected space persists across the sibling tabs.

screens.name: space-members
screens.reason: The Members tab reads memberships and pending invitations for the same selected space and manages member roles.

screens.name: invite-space-member
screens.reason: The Space Members reading retains the selected space and its memberships, making it the nearest qualifying context. The invitation collects an invitee and role within that context. Changing the selected space replaces the reading and ends this invitation.

screens.name: create-access-token
screens.reason: A new-token process collecting description and expiry, followed by the generated credential reveal on the same Screen. The token list merely launches this process; a generated credential reveal is explicitly an Outcome, including its copy control.

screens.name: member-editor
screens.reason: Create/update form selects a member or new-member draft. The list merely opens it; creation versus update is a behavior condition of the same editor.

screens.name: webhook-editor
screens.reason: Creates or edits a selected webhook and manages its secret. The collection opens this destination without a persistent selected webhook reading.

screens.name: identity-provider-editor
screens.reason: Creates or edits a selected identity provider. Provider templates and type-dependent form fields are behavior conditions, not extra Screens.

screens.name: ai-provider-editor
screens.reason: Edits one provider within the persistent instance AI configuration reading. The nearest qualifying context is AI Settings. On save it persists the providers while deliberately preserving any separate transcription draft; it is not an intermediate save of that transcription draft.

screens.name: instance-profile
screens.reason: Edits the profile of the same instance being configured; this subform retains the instance subject.

screens.name: memo-import-review
screens.reason: Retains the staged file and operation while asking for conflict policy and the decision to import or cancel. This satisfies the explicit Actor-decision stage test; the completed report does not create another child.

uncertainties: Screen identity remains open for memo composition: one shared drafting/editing Screen is proposed across Home creation, inline memo edits, global composition and comment creation. The new parent rules do not determine whether these distinct purposes are one Product place or several, and component reuse cannot decide that. Their link/location ownership depends on this identity decision.

The boundary between a persistent configuration subject and a list that only launches a destination remains material. This inventory treats AI Settings and Instance Settings as ongoing readings of one instance configuration, but Members, Webhooks and Identity Providers as collections launching independently selected editors. A current-account or instance scope is available to all of them. The new rules exclude generic selectors but do not determine when implicit singleton account/instance context qualifies as a selected subject.

Nearest qualifying context gives a parent only after Screen identity and qualifying contexts are settled. For example, this inventory places Invite Space Member beneath Space Members because that tab still reads a particular space membership set. Source implementation instead instantiates the dialog in SpaceDetail; implementation containment is not Product ownership.

Space Detail is retained as the persistent selected-space reading above its General and Members tabs. The header reads space identity; a complete model must place a real Capability on the parent as well as its children. The rubric does not settle whether that header-only parent is a separate stable place or whether one tab should supply the parent reading.
Image preview and audio player are proposed attachment-reading Screens. Stable view versus control/expanded drawing remains a granularity call that the ownership additions do not decide.

Scope remains Home, MemoDetail, Settings and related memo/editor/settings dialogs; other routes were read only to resolve shared ownership. Global Quick Find and user-preference dialogs are outside this page-owned scope. No Capability model was authored, so per-Screen placed-Capability validity was not tested.
